name: The Lethe Hollow

detectability.signature: A flat silence in the graviton background: perfectly empty readings where stars still shine

proximity: Navigation solutions wander as plotted position drifts from true position
Star trackers lose lock as background alignments shift across the boundary
contact: Artificial gravity and inertial dampers stutter and drop out
Vessels coast uncontrollably, engines pushing against nothing
prolonged_exposure: Permanent miscalibration of inertial guidance systems
Crew disorientation severe enough to induce nausea and panic

phenomena: Objects decelerating without thrust as they cross the boundary
Inverted gravitational lensing: background stars drifting slowly out of alignment
Instrument masses reading zero while cargo remains stubbornly heavy
hazards: Navigation system failure inside the null volume
Collision risk from undetected mass drifting through the void
opportunities: Hidden base location; the Hollow swallows sensor emissions
Smuggling route effectively invisible to pursuit
known_incidents: The patrol cutter Stern Watch chased a smuggler into the Hollow and emerged with her forward battery crushed by something neither craft ever registered
Nineteen mapping expeditions have produced nineteen different boundaries
description: There is nothing to see. The Lethe Hollow occupies a planetary-scale sphere of space where gravity simply does not answer, a hole in the fabric that pulls nothing, holds nothing, and explains itself to no instrument. Stars shine through it normally; only their subtle misalignment across the boundary betrays that something is profoundly wrong.

Crossing in, ships feel lighter by degrees until inertial systems lose all reference and every object coasts in eerie obedience to Newton alone. The boundary itself wanders, sometimes tens of thousands of kilometers between one week and the next, which makes the Hollow as dangerous as it is quiet. Instruments recalibrated inside rarely trust themselves again.

Stellar survey flagged the region two centuries ago after a string of unpowered collisions that involved no collision courses. Since then it has been mapped nineteen times and defined twenty different ways. Physicists argue whether the Hollow is a scar left by some primordial cancellation of mass or a bubble of excluded spacetime; the data politely supports everyone.

Smugglers love it, garrisons hate it, and no two charts agree on its current edge. Anyone can hide here, including things better left unmet. The Hollow asks nothing of those who enter, which is precisely what makes veterans uneasy.
